text:
alice: heads up — found a reproducible race where the async python client retries after a timeout and ends up creating the same resource twice. unsure if backoff config or typing bug. anyone seen this?

alice: minimal gist below (using 0.9.3):
```python
# repro_async_resend.py
from uuid import uuid4
from redwood import RedwoodAsyncClient

client = RedwoodAsyncClient(api_key=... , timeout=2)

async def make_one():
    idemp = str(uuid4())
    # non-idempotent POST to /v1/objects (example)
    await client.post('/v1/objects', json={"name": "test"}, headers={"Idempotency-Key": idemp}, retry_policy={"max_retries": 3, "backoff_factor": 0.3})

# run this twice concurrently against a flaky infra that returns 504 on one attempt
```

alice: behavior: server returns 201 created on first attempt, then connection times out for the client -> client retries and server processes a second create -> duplicate object. I expected either no retry (for non-idempotent by default) or the SDK to preserve headers/idempotency keys across replay.

ben: which SDK version again? you said 0.9.3? there was a change around async retry plumbing last month. can you paste the raw request/response headers from your logs?

alice: yep 0.9.3. logs: 
```
OUT: POST /v1/objects 201 id=req_ABC123 headers: {Idempotency-Key: a1}
OUT: client timeout waiting for response (read timeout)
OUT: retry #1 -> POST /v1/objects  -> 201 id=req_DEF456 headers: {Idempotency-Key: a1}
```

carla: hmm. two quick notes: 1) async client recipe didn't automatically inject Idempotency-Key for POSTs the same way sync client does (we debated that), 2) the retry_policy param is typed in the async constructor as Union[RetryPolicy, None] but the public builder accepts dicts — I bet pydantic/type-checking is silently converting the dict into a plain dict and the retry codepath checks isinstance(retry_policy, RetryPolicy) before applying backoff so it falls back to immediate retries.

carla: workaround: explicitly construct the RetryPolicy object or set headers yourself. e.g.
```python
from redwood.retry import RetryPolicy
policy = RetryPolicy(max_retries=3, backoff_factor=0.5)
await client.post(..., retry_policy=policy)
```

alice: confirmed workaround works locally. thanks. will open a tiny PR to make the async client accept dicts (or coerce them) and preserve headers across replays.

ben: please include a test that simulates a half-closed socket + 504/timeout path so we cover replay. also add a note in changelog — this is a subtle DX trap for users who assume dict config will be accepted like other SDKs.

carla: also add a typing hint in the constructor: retry_policy: RetryPolicy | dict | None and a runtime coercion helper. avoid widening to Any.

alice: filing issue + PR in a few hours. assigning to @ben for review.

ci-bot: CI queued for branch alice/async-replay-fix (tests: unit, lint)

ci-bot: unit tests started (job id 4921)

ben: thanks. once CI passes we should cut a patch release. this one can cause duplicated resources in production for customers not using Idempotency-Key.

carla: maybe add a short note in the quickstart for async clients about idempotency header differences until patch is cut.

alice: yup will update quickstart too. thanks all :thumbsup:
